import polars as pl
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style
from great_tables.data import gtcars

# This is `gtcars`
pl.from_pandas(gtcars).glimpse()

# Get a subset of 8 cars from the `gtcars` dataset: two
# from each manufacturer country of origin except the UK
gtcars_8 = (
    pl.from_pandas(gtcars)
    .filter(pl.int_range(pl.len()).over("ctry_origin") < 2)
    .sort("ctry_origin", maintain_order=True)
    .filter(pl.col("ctry_origin") != "United Kingdom")
)

# Show the `gtcars_8` table
gtcars_8.glimpse()

# Use `groupname_col` on `gtcars_8` to make row groups
GT(gtcars_8, groupname_col="ctry_origin")

# Define our preferred order for `ctry_origin`
order_countries = ["Germany", "Italy", "United States", "Japan"]
# (a country not in the list comes last, as R's `factor()` does)
country_rank = pl.col("ctry_origin").replace_strict(
    order_countries, list(range(len(order_countries))), default=len(order_countries)
)

# Reorder the table rows by our specific ordering of groups
GT(
    gtcars_8.sort(
        country_rank, "mfr", "msrp",
        descending=[False, False, True],
    ),
    groupname_col="ctry_origin",
)

# Reorder the table rows by our specific ordering of groups
tab = GT(
    gtcars_8.sort(
        country_rank, "mfr", "msrp",
        descending=[False, False, True],
    )
    .with_columns(car=pl.concat_str("mfr", "model", separator=" "))
    .drop("mfr", "model"),
    rowname_col="car",
    groupname_col="ctry_origin",
)

# Show the table
tab

# Use a few `cols_*()` methods to hide and move columns
tab = (
    tab
    .cols_hide(columns=["drivetrain", "bdy_style"])
    .cols_move(columns=["trsmn", "mpg_c", "mpg_h"], after="trim")
)

# Show the table
tab

# Put the first three columns under a spanner
# column with the label 'Performance'
tab = tab.tab_spanner(
    label="Performance",
    columns=["mpg_c", "mpg_h", "hp", "hp_rpm", "trq", "trq_rpm"],
)

# Show the table
tab

# Perform three column merges to better present # MPG, HP, and torque; relabel all the remaining # columns for a nicer-looking presentation tab = ( tab .cols_merge(columns=["mpg_c", "mpg_h"], pattern="<<{0}c
{1}h>>") .cols_merge(columns=["hp", "hp_rpm"], pattern="{0}
@{1}rpm") .cols_merge(columns=["trq", "trq_rpm"], pattern="{0}
@{1}rpm") .cols_label( mpg_c="MPG", hp="HP", trq="Torque", year="Year", trim="Trim", trsmn="Transmission", msrp="MSRP", ) ) # Show the table tab

# Format the `msrp` column to USD currency
# with no display of the currency subunits
tab = tab.fmt_currency(columns="msrp", decimals=0)

# Show the table
tab

# Center-align three columns in the table and
# modify the text size of a few columns of data
tab = (
    tab
    .cols_align(align="center", columns=["mpg_c", "hp", "trq"])
    .tab_style(
        style=style.text(size="12px"),
        locations=loc.body(columns=["trim", "trsmn", "mpg_c", "hp", "trq"]),
    )
)

# Show the table
tab

# Transform the text in `trsmn` with a function # given to `text_transform()`; here `x` is the # formatted text of one cell def transmission(x): # The first character of `x` always # indicates the number of transmission speeds speed = x[0] # Which transmission type we have in `x` if x[1:3] == "am": type = "Automatic/Manual" elif x[1] == "m": type = "Manual" elif x[1] == "a": type = "Automatic" elif x[1:3] == "dd": type = "Direct Drive" # The speed and the type, as HTML text replacing `x` return f"{speed} Speed
{type}" tab = tab.text_transform(locations=loc.body(columns="trsmn"), fn=transmission) # Show the table tab

# Add a table title and subtitle; we can use
# Markdown with the `md()` helper function
tab = tab.tab_header(
    title=md("The Cars of **gtcars**"),
    subtitle="These are some fine automobiles",
)

# Show the table
tab

# Add a source note to the bottom of the table; this
# appears below the footnotes
tab = tab.tab_source_note(
    source_note=md("Source: Various pages within the Edmonds website.")
)

# Show the table
tab

# The car with the best city gas mileage, and the one with the # highest horsepower: they will be used to target the correct # cells for footnotes cars_named = pl.from_pandas(gtcars).with_columns( car=pl.concat_str("mfr", "model", separator=" ") ) best_gas_mileage_city = cars_named.top_k(1, by="mpg_c")["car"].to_list() highest_horsepower = cars_named.top_k(1, by="hp")["car"].to_list() # Define our preferred order for `ctry_origin` order_countries = ["Germany", "Italy", "United States", "Japan"] # Create a display table with `gtcars`, using all of the previous # methods chained together + additional `tab_footnote()` calls tab = ( GT( pl.from_pandas(gtcars) .sort( country_rank, "mfr", "msrp", descending=[False, False, True], ) .with_columns(car=pl.concat_str("mfr", "model", separator=" ")) .drop("mfr", "model"), rowname_col="car", groupname_col="ctry_origin", ) .cols_hide(columns=["drivetrain", "bdy_style"]) .cols_move(columns=["trsmn", "mpg_c", "mpg_h"], after="trim") .tab_spanner( label="Performance", columns=["mpg_c", "mpg_h", "hp", "hp_rpm", "trq", "trq_rpm"], ) .cols_merge(columns=["mpg_c", "mpg_h"], pattern="<<{0}c
{1}h>>") .cols_merge(columns=["hp", "hp_rpm"], pattern="{0}
@{1}rpm") .cols_merge(columns=["trq", "trq_rpm"], pattern="{0}
@{1}rpm") .cols_label( mpg_c="MPG", hp="HP", trq="Torque", year="Year", trim="Trim", trsmn="Transmission", msrp="MSRP", ) .fmt_currency(columns="msrp", decimals=0) .cols_align(align="center", columns=["mpg_c", "hp", "trq"]) .tab_style( style=style.text(size="12px"), locations=loc.body(columns=["trim", "trsmn", "mpg_c", "hp", "trq"]), ) .text_transform(locations=loc.body(columns="trsmn"), fn=transmission) .tab_header( title=md("The Cars of **gtcars**"), subtitle="These are some fine automobiles", ) .tab_source_note( source_note=md("Source: Various pages within the Edmonds website.") ) .tab_footnote( footnote=md("Best gas mileage (city) of all the **gtcars**."), locations=loc.body( columns="mpg_c", rows=pl.col("car").is_in(best_gas_mileage_city) ), ) .tab_footnote( footnote=md("The highest horsepower of all the **gtcars**."), locations=loc.body( columns="hp", rows=pl.col("car").is_in(highest_horsepower) ), ) .tab_footnote( footnote="All prices in U.S. dollars (USD).", locations=loc.column_labels(columns="msrp"), ) ) # Show the table tab
